events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 8 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The driver cancelled the trip at 09:15:05 himself (cancelled_by = driver), so the $5.00 cancelled-trip charge can only stand if the driver proves a rider no-show under NS-1; the driver does not dispute that he cancelled, so NS-0 routes this to NS-1/NS-2. [F4 F12] [NS-0 NS-1 NS-2]
C2: NS-1's conditions are read on the record's own no-show threshold of 8 minutes, and the driver's own written statement and chat message both rely on that 8-minute rule, not on 3 minutes. [F12 F10] [NS-1]
C3: Conditions (i) and (ii) are met: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:07:15 while 40 m from the pickup point — inside the 200 m arrival radius — and the platform separately recorded arrival at 09:06:20. [F6 F5] [NS-1]
C4: Condition (iii) is satisfied as well: the driver sat stationary 41 m from the pickup point from 09:06:55 until he cancelled at 09:15:05 — 8 min 10 s of continuous waiting at the pickup, and 7 min 50 s within 200 m after the tap — i.e. the full 8-minute threshold was already complete when he cancelled. [F3 F6 F2 F4] [NS-1]
C5: The rider's own message-side account (that she came out about a minute after the cancellation) does not defeat the charge, because the record shows the driver had already waited out the entire threshold before cancelling; the rider shows no toll, waiting-fee or other unpublished add-on to attack separately, and the ride was never completed so NS-6 does not apply. [F2 F3 F4 F7] [NS-1 NS-6]
C6: No GPS gap is present: the track has sampling that covers the waiting period and runs up to the cancellation moment (closest approach 32 m at 09:06:50; stationary continuously until 09:15:05), so NS-1's gap carve-out and the incomplete-evidence rule do not force this case to a human. [F1 F3 F4 F6] [NS-1]
C7: Because all three NS-1 conditions hold, the $6.61/$5.00 cancellation charge as recorded is correctly founded and the outcome on the charge is no_action; the case record shows no basis for a rider-side refund or fee waiver. [F4 F7] [NS-1 NS-2]
C8: Although no-show branch is against the rider, the driver's flag request is not available: the driver complied with the arrival/waiver conditions (tap 40 m from pickup, stationary 41 m away until cancellation), so NS-2's abuse-of-button flag does not trigger, and the driver's account remains an account-review matter only if Ryde sees a 90-day repeat pattern, not a finding of this case. [F6 F3 F17] [NS-1 NS-2 RD-6]
Weaknesses: The rider has no system evidence contradicting the driver's wait: F3 (stationary 09:06:55-09:15:05, 41 m from pickup) and F6 (tap at 09:07:15, 7 min 50 s within 200 m after tap) satisfy NS-1(iii) outright, so the honest answer on the fee is that the charge stands. | F10 (driver's 09:14 message "8 min up, cancelling the trip") and F12 (his statement that he waited the full 8 minutes) are corroborated by the GPS rather than contradicted by it, so the usual argument that driver statements lose to records does not help the rider here. | If the judge chooses the default 3-minute threshold in NS-1 rather than the record's 8-minute threshold, the wait was still 8 min 10 s and the charge stands — the rider gains nothing either way from the threshold choice. | Rider's 90-day history (F16: 1 dispute, 0 upheld) is neutral at best, and the driver (F17: 1 no-show dispute upheld in 90 d) means a repeat-pattern argument, if the judge were to apply RD-6 logic, would point the other way. | The rider's complaint wording gives a soft time ('a minute after the driver cancelled') that is not backed by any timestamped rider message in the chat (F9-F11 contain only driver messages), so we cannot prove she was at the pickup before the cancellation.
Asks: no_action

The rider's own message-side account (that she came out about a minute after the cancellation) does not defeat the charge, because the record shows the driver had already waited out the entire threshold before cancelling; the rider shows no toll, waiting-fee or other unpublished add-on to attack separately, and the ride was never completed so NS-6 does not apply.

No GPS gap is present: the track has sampling that covers the waiting period and runs up to the cancellation moment (closest approach 32 m at 09:06:50; stationary continuously until 09:15:05), so NS-1's gap carve-out and the incomplete-evidence rule do not force this case to a human.

After the tap the driver remained within 200 m of the pickup for 7 min 50 s and was stationary just 41 m from the pickup from 09:06:55 until the cancellation at 09:15:05 — well beyond the 3-minute continuous-wait requirement.

The driver gave the rider notice while waiting ("I'm here at the pickup point" at 09:07, then "8 min up, cancelling the trip" at 09:14); the chat record contains 2 timestamped messages and is complete, so the wait and cancellation are documented, not fabricated.

The rider's account of coming out "a minute after" the cancellation does not displace the system record: the driver was within 200 m of the pickup for 8 min 45 s and stationary on station for 8 min 10 s, and the rider never messaged the driver to say she was coming out.
Because the no-show conditions were satisfied, the cancellation fee on record of $5.00 stands and no refund is owed; the rider's complaint should be dismissed.

Conditions (i) and (ii) are met: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:07:15 while 40 m from the pickup point — inside the 200 m arrival radius — and the platform separately recorded arrival at 09:06:20.

Condition (iii) is satisfied as well: the driver sat stationary 41 m from the pickup point from 09:06:55 until he cancelled at 09:15:05 — 8 min 10 s of continuous waiting at the pickup, and 7 min 50 s within 200 m after the tap — i.e. the full 8-minute threshold was already complete when he cancelled.

The rider's own message-side account (that she came out about a minute after the cancellation) does not defeat the charge, because the record shows the driver had already waited out the entire threshold before cancelling; the rider shows no toll, waiting-fee or other unpublished add-on to attack separately, and the ride was never completed so NS-6 does not apply.

F10 (driver's 09:14 message "8 min up, cancelling the trip") and F12 (his statement that he waited the full 8 minutes) are corroborated by the GPS rather than contradicted by it, so the usual argument that driver statements lose to records does not help the rider here.

If the judge chooses the default 3-minute threshold in NS-1 rather than the record's 8-minute threshold, the wait was still 8 min 10 s and the charge stands — the rider gains nothing either way from the threshold choice.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:07:15 while 40 m from the pickup point, so the arrival condition of NS-1(i) is met and the tap was truthful, not an abuse of the button.

After the tap the driver remained within 200 m of the pickup for 7 min 50 s and was stationary just 41 m from the pickup from 09:06:55 until the cancellation at 09:15:05 — well beyond the 3-minute continuous-wait requirement.

The platform's own timeline records the driver arrival at 09:06:20 and the cancellation 8 min 45 s later, and no GPS gap or uncovered track interval appears before cancellation, so the wait can be relied on rather than referred to a human.

The driver gave the rider notice while waiting ("I'm here at the pickup point" at 09:07, then "8 min up, cancelling the trip" at 09:14); the chat record contains 2 timestamped messages and is complete, so the wait and cancellation are documented, not fabricated.

The rider's account of coming out "a minute after" the cancellation does not displace the system record: the driver was within 200 m of the pickup for 8 min 45 s and stationary on station for 8 min 10 s, and the rider never messaged the driver to say she was coming out.
Because the no-show conditions were satisfied, the cancellation fee on record of $5.00 stands and no refund is owed; the rider's complaint should be dismissed.
No safety escalation is triggered: nothing in the chat, statement or complaint reads as a threat, harassment or a dangerous-driving allegation.

Even on the rider's best case there is no account flag against the driver — he was at the pickup when he tapped and the profile shows only one prior upheld no-show dispute, the issue being resolved by NS-1 rather than any abuse finding.

weaknesses: The rider's core factual assertion (F4 context / complaint) is that she came out within a minute of the cancellation; the timeline (F5) shows the cancellation at 09:15:05, so a claim that she arrived at 09:16:05 would be one minute late only if uncorroborated — but there is no GPS or timeline fact recording the rider's own arrival time, so her timing is neither confirmed nor refuted by system records.

The driver's own written statement (F12) refers to "the full 8 minutes the rule gives" and no fact in the table records an official no_show_threshold_min of 8 for this case; if the judge applies the NS-1 default (over 3 minutes) the outcome is the same, but the statement's premise is not backed by a record.

F7 shows the fee charged was $5.00, whereas the published cancellation fee under NS-0 is $6.61; the rider's complaint uses the $5.00 figure, so the judge may question which fee was actually imposed and whether the fare record is inconsistent.

The driver's rating (4.48, F17) is below the rider's (4.7, F16), and F17 shows 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days against him — the rider's side may use this to argue a pattern of premature cancellations, although RD-6 only allows profile facts as a supplementary account-review trigger, not as proof of this case.

points.response: Conceded — F1 (32 m closest approach) and F2 (first within 200 m at 09:06:20) do establish the NS-1(ii) arrival location, and I do not contest it.
Conceded — F6 shows the tap at 09:07:15 at 40 m from the pickup, so NS-1(i) is met and the tap was accurate, not an abuse of the button under NS-2.

Conceded — F3 (stationary 09:06:55–09:15:05, 41 m from pickup) and F6 (7 min 50 s inside 200 m after the tap) satisfy NS-1(iii) on either the 8-minute or the default reading, so my client does not get the fee back.

Accepted with one correction: F3/F6 show no GPS gap and track coverage up to the 09:15:05 cancellation, so NS-1's gap carve-out does not apply — but this supports the driver, not my client, and my brief already conceded the charge stands.

Not contested as to documentation — F9, F10 and F11 are two timestamped messages in a complete record — but the chat contains only driver messages, so it documents the driver's wait, not any rider no-show notice given to her before he pulled the plug.

Half-conceded: F2/F3 do outweigh the rider's uncorroborated timing, but F11 shows only two driver messages and no rider reply, so 'the rider never messaged' is the absence of a record on both sides rather than proof she ignored a notice — the notice element is not a NS-1 condition in any event.

Conceded on the charge: NS-1's conditions hold on F3/F4/F6, so the fee on record stands and my revised outcome remains no_action; the only discrepancy is that F7 records $5.00 rather than the published $6.61, which is a fare-record question for Ryde, not a rider refund.
Conceded — F9, F10 and F12 contain no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so neither SAFE-1 nor SAFE-2 sends this case to a human.

Conceded on the flag: F6 and F3 show the driver tapped and waited legitimately, so NS-2's abuse flag against him is unavailable, and F17's single upheld no-show dispute cannot by itself prove anything about this trip under RD-6.
Agreed on the routing: the driver cancelled (F4, F12), so NS-0 sends the case to NS-1, and NS-1 places the charge in his favour once (i)/(ii)/(iii) hold.

Immaterial to my client: whether the judge reads the default "over 3 minutes" or an 8-minute record threshold, the driver's wait of 7 min 50 s inside 200 m after the tap and 8 min 10 s stationary (F3, F6) clears either figure, so nothing turns on the threshold the opponent invokes from F10/F12.

Accepted without reservation: the tap at 09:07:15 at 40 m and the platform-recorded arrival at 09:06:20 (F5, F6) satisfy NS-1(i) and (ii), which is exactly why NS-2's abuse-of-button flag is unavailable against my client.

Correct, and this is the decisive point: the GPS record (F3) shows the vehicle parked 41 m from the pickup from 09:06:55 to 09:15:05, so the continuous wait ran to the cancellation itself (F4) and NS-1(iii) is satisfied on system records, not on the driver's word.

The rider's soft timing cannot displace the system record: she was inside the arrival radius for 8 min 45 s (F2) and no message from her appears in the chat (F9, F10, F11), and NS-1 turns on the driver's wait, so the $5.00 charge stands.

Agreed: continuous sampling from the closest approach at 09:06:50 through the stationary period to 09:15:05 (F1, F3) leaves no gap, so NS-1's gap carve-out and the missing-evidence referral are not engaged.
Both sides now agree the only defensible disposition of the $5.00 charge is no_action, and F7 shows no other sum to refund.
The driver never sought a flag against anyone; my D9 asserted only that none should attach to him, so I concede this point insofar as no account action is requested on this record (F6, F17).
